instrument: ECOnorthwest / UVA Weldon Cooper Center, Understanding Oregon's Data Center Industry (preliminary, July 31, 2026)
summary: Preliminary modeled estimate: Oregon data center electricity demand of 14.0 TWh in 2025 rising to 24.8 TWh by 2030, built from installed IT power, utilization, PUE, hours and load factor using S&P Global 451 Research facility data. 111 operational facilities, 32 future.
text: Estimated data center electricity demand rises from 14.0 TWh in 2025 to 24.8 TWh by 2030. [...] For 2026 onward, the right-hand chart compares data center demand with Oregon's electricity-demand level in 2025.

source.citation: ECOnorthwest and University of Virginia Weldon Cooper Center, Understanding Oregon's Data Center Industry: An Evidence Based Assessment, preliminary findings presented to the Oregon Data Center Advisory Committee, July 31, 2026

notes: Coverage conflict. The widely reported 22.8% of 2025 retail electricity sales does not appear in this deck; it is attributed to the final 135-page report (released September 17, 2026, Lemelson Foundation funded; not located). Coverage has drifted the denominator from retail sales to consumption to demand, and rounded to 'nearly 25%'. KGW's 'nearly triple by 2030' does not reconcile: 14.0 to 24.8 TWh is 1.77x. The 2030 share (~31-32%) divides future data center demand by 2025 statewide demand. Washington County figures in the deck: $20.58 million in data center property tax, ~1.2% of total collection; data center employment ~0.09%. The deck's Washington County includes incorporated cities; do not compare it with the county's unincorporated-only parcel analysis.
